name: Should I replace the entire vanity cabinet or just the countertop and sink?

mainEntity.name: Should I replace the entire vanity cabinet or just the countertop and sink?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing an entire vanity makes sense if the cabinet structure has water damage, poor storage, or an outdated layout, whereas a countertop swap works if the box remains solid. If your current cabinet features sturdy, solid-wood construction and a layout that serves your daily routine, replacing just the sink, faucet, and countertop gives a modern look for less disruption. However, if the cabinet box is constructed of swollen particle board, lacks functional drawers, or sits at an uncomfortably low height, full replacement is the better long-term choice.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace just the countertop if the existing cabinet box is sturdy and functional. Replace the entire unit if the cabinet shows water damage or has an impractical layout.
